observations.finding: 2013 p.223 describes the English Cybersemiotics title as a foundational book and cites (Brier, 2006). A genuine same-title 2006 English doctoral thesis is catalogued separately from the 2008 UTP book; the 2013 bibliography omits the thesis. The intended manifestation cannot be resolved.

2013 p.259 lists Brier (2006) as Danish Informationsvidenskabsteori, second edition, and English Cybersemiotics as Brier (2008a). It omits the catalogued 2006 English thesis and does not list the 2006 Semiotica article under that label.

2013 p.224 four-views discussion cites Brier 2006; the 2013 bibliography supplies Danish textbook as that label, but does not resolve whether the intended underlying source is that text, 2006 English thesis or another manifestation; no Semiotica link established.
Publisher gives DOI 10.1515/SEM.2006.008, printed 20 February 2006, online 28 April 2006 and an abstract listing five levels; it explicitly reports article-body access unavailable.

CBS copy includes one repository title-page cover; printed p.81 occurs at PDF index 11, whereas journal-hosted manifestation in accepted R007 ledger has p.81 at index 10. Both are valid only for their own URL.
CBS catalogues an English 2006 doctoral thesis Cybersemiotics: Why information is not enough, 544 pages, print ISBN 8759399864; no original thesis body or pages were inspected.
CBS separately catalogues the University of Toronto Press 2008 English book, 477 pages, print ISBN 9780802092205 and electronic ISBN 9781442687813; original book text was not inspected.

Brier's dated 2013 CV first page calls the 2008 UTP work an improved version and mentions a 2010 edition with minor changes, but also uses Danish-dissertation phrasing requiring caution; no textual comparison performed.

scope: Selected journal-PDF pages (2013 pp.223/224/259; 2003 p.81), first page of dated author CV, Semiotica publisher abstract, and CBS institutional catalogue metadata only. No original local PDF bytes/SHA, full 2006 Semiotica or thesis body, 2008 UTP book reading, full article reading, independent human review or selected Track G corpus.
